speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, rhinorrhea, and headache; have you noticed any other skin changes like a rash spreading to your palms or soles? Also, has anyone around you been diagnosed with chickenpox or shingles recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease)

The description of a facial rash sparing the perioral area appearing after a viral prodrome is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. I will now request blood work to confirm the presence of Parvovirus B19 IgM antibodies. REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus_B19_IgM
